# skopli

TypeScript SDK that reads real AI coding-agent usage (tokens, sessions, turns, calls) from local harness state, aggregates it, and prices it against market catalogs (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, models.dev). ESM only, Node >= 24.

## Layers

1. Read (offline): `detectHarnesses()`, `readUsage({ harnesses?, since?, until?, tz?, subagents?, home?, env? })` -> `{ events, diagnostics, skipped }`. UsageEvent = { harness, timestamp, sessionId, messageId, turn, subagent, model, tokens: { input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, cacheWrite1h?, reasoning }, calls?, costUsd?, workspace?, title? }. cacheWrite is the total; cacheWrite1h is the 1h-TTL portion when the source reports the split (claude). costUsd is the harness-recorded cost (claude jsonl costUSD, opencode nonzero cost); absent otherwise. workspace (normalized project dir, cross-platform: forward slashes, no trailing sep, case-folded on Windows) and title come from opencode session directory/title and claude cwd; absent otherwise. Subagent (child-session/sidechain) events are included and tagged `subagent: true` by default; `subagents: "exclude"` drops them uniformly. `subagent` is set from each harness's native marker: opencode non-null parent_id/parentID, claude strict isSidechain === true, pi/omp rlmDepth > 0, codex and all other harnesses always false. The SDK never writes to stdio; problems are structured diagnostics.
2. Rollup: `rollup(events, { by: "model" | "day" | "session" | "harness" | "workspace", tz? })` -> sorted `Rollup[]` with summed tokens, events, turns, calls, and costUsd (summed recorded cost, present only when an event carried one). Day bucketing is timezone-aware; workspace bucketing folds events without a workspace under the "(unknown)" sentinel.
3. Price (network, opt-in): `createPricing({ sources?, overrides?, mode?, cacheDir?, offline?, ttlMs?, refresh?, fetch? })` -> `{ lookupModel, priceTokens, priceRollups, priceEvents, catalogs }`. Priority: overrides > OpenRouter > LiteLLM > models.dev, with one exception - after overrides, any tier-bearing match outranks a flat (tier-less) match from a higher-priority source, so long-context tiers are not lost to a higher-priority flat source (in practice this is the tiered LiteLLM catalog beating flat OpenRouter). mode ("calculate" default | "display" | "auto") picks each priceRollups usd: calculate recomputes from tokens, display uses the recorded cost or 0, auto prefers recorded then calculated. `priceRollups(rollups)` prices already-summed tokens - exact for flat-rate models, but for a tiered model whose rollup aggregated more than one event (or a single event that itself aggregates multiple calls, calls > 1) the summed context can cross a tier the individual calls never reached, overbilling; that row is flagged `pricing.tieredAggregate: true` (calculate mode, or auto without a recorded cost) so it is never a silent misprice. `priceEvents(events, { by, tz? })` -> `PricedEventGroup[]` is the correct path for tiered models: it prices each event at its own context (per-event tier selection) with the full tiered/1h-split logic, applies mode per event, then aggregates per group with the same keys as `rollup` - a group prices only when every member model priced. Provenance: a single-model group returns a `PriceHit` (its real model, key, price, source); a multi-model group (possible under by session/day/harness/workspace) returns `AggregatePriceHit` ({ priced: true, usd, models }) instead of claiming one model's rate. A single-model group whose events aggregate multiple calls (calls > 1) on a tiered model is still flagged `tieredAggregate: true`, since per-call tokens are not separable. Per-source disk cache (~1h TTL, atomic writes, any-age stale fallback); `refresh: true` attempts one fresh fetch per source, bypassing fresh caches, with stale-cache fallback on failure; default fetches abort after 10s. `catalogs()` reports loaded-source provenance. Results carry source attribution and fetchedAt. Prices are USD per million tokens.

## Model matching

Tiered: exact -> provider-prefix strip (openai/gpt-5 -> gpt-5) -> family aliases (some platforms resell a model line under their own route prefix, e.g. duo-chat-opus-4-6 -> claude-opus-4.6, so those names price as the underlying Claude model) -> separator/date normalization (claude-sonnet-4.5 ~ claude-sonnet-4-5 ~ claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) -> provider-prefixed family forms (claude-opus-4.6 -> anthropic/claude-opus-4.6, how OpenRouter keys Claude) -> alias table (hand-maintained, for names the mechanical tiers miss). Misses return { priced: false, attempted } instead of guessing. Zero-cost catalog entries are treated as placeholders and skipped so matching falls through to the next source; when only zero-cost entries match, the result is { priced: false, reason: "zeroCost", key }. An explicit $0 in `overrides` is honored as a real price, not skipped.

## Supported harnesses

claude, opencode, codex, gemini, copilot, amp, droid, qwen, pi, omp, kilo, goose, hermes, kimi, openclaw, junie, grok, augment, codebuff, codebuddy, jcode, mux, zed, zcode, devin, roo, cline, kilocode, prime, gajae, kimchi, mimocode, commandcode, cherrystudio, opencodereview, trae, deepseek, reasonix. Detected but unsupported (no reliable local token data): Cursor, aider, Kiro, Crush, GitLab Duo CLI.

## Semantics worth knowing

- Date-only since/until strings (YYYY-MM-DD) are interpreted in tz (default: system timezone, matching rollup's day bucketing); since = start of day, until = exclusive end of day. Full ISO timestamps are used exactly as given. West of UTC this matters: with tz America/Los_Angeles, since "2026-08-01" excludes an event at 2026-08-01T00:30Z (17:30 Jul 31 local), so a day rollup in that tz never shows a "2026-07-31" row.
- Zero-token rows are dropped regardless of vendor-reported cost.
- Unusable timestamps warn and skip, never epoch-0.
- calls aggregation uses the reported count only when finite, else 1 per event.
- Reasoning tokens bill as output; cache price tiers fall back to the input rate when a catalog omits them.
- Codex, Grok, and ZCode report reasoning inside their output count, so the reader subtracts reasoning from output (output + reasoning reconstructs the source's raw output). Copilot OTel is the deliberate exception: the OTel GenAI conventions do not state whether output_tokens includes reasoning, so the reader assumes they are disjoint and does not subtract; if Copilot output turns out to be reasoning-inclusive, its reasoning would be double-billed.
- Codex cache-write tokens come from cache_write_input_tokens (2026-07 protocol addition), a disjoint subset of input_tokens like cache reads, so the reader subtracts them from input (input = raw_input - cacheRead - cacheWrite) and emits them as tokens.cacheWrite; absent in older session files = 0.
- 1h cache writes (tokens.cacheWrite1h) bill at the catalog above-1hr rate (LiteLLM cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_1hr) when present, else input x 2.0; the rest of cacheWrite bills at the base cacheWrite rate. Source priority is per-model, not per-field.
- Long-context tiers (LiteLLM only): tier chosen by total context (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite); marginal billing by default, whole-request repricing for claude models. The cacheWrite 5m/1h split composes per tier: the 1h portion bills at the selected level's 1h rate, the 5m remainder at its cacheWrite rate.
- Cross-store dedup: sqlite stores are authoritative over legacy jsonl mirrors (opencode, zcode, devin, cline).
